debate_title: Should governments break up vertically integrated AI comp...

conflicts.point: Whether structural unbundling of compute, cloud, and model layers is necessary to prevent monopolistic gatekeeping or whether it destroys essential technical integration and slows deployment.

positions.stance: Antitrust agencies must aggressively break up cloud computing, chip supply, and model design before a small oligopoly controls the entire machine learning stack.
Structural separation introduces regulatory friction that halts progress by destroying the co-designed hardware and training loops needed for rapid technological advancement.

verdicts.conflict: Whether structural unbundling of compute, cloud, and model layers is necessary to prevent monopolistic gatekeeping or whether it destroys essential technical integration and slows deployment.
verdicts.rationale: Both camps present verifiable facts—cloud concentration metrics are empirically documented, while historical precedents like the Linux kernel demonstrate decentralized software distribution. However, neither side provides direct empirical data on whether breaking up vertically integrated AI stacks specifically would enhance or destroy frontier model development speeds.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Longitudinal performance and deployment data from markets where cloud and model layers are legally separated versus vertically integrated.
